joern.classification: Allocation and cleanup are intended ownership transitions; the final kfree is a confirmed dangling-slot path when vmalloc fails.

canonical_build.reason: No source or Kbuild input changed; the Docker report includes this unchanged C mirror in the curated source tree, while Kbuild selects preserved exact assembly.

findings.details: After storing the descriptor at cdev+0xc58, vmalloc failure logs and kfree's it, then returns -ENOMEM without storing NULL to cdev+0xc58. A later call can read the dangling slot and dereference freed descriptor memory during initial cleanup, with possible invalid vfree or repeated free depending on reused contents.

evidence.ghidra_decompilation: decompiled/0011_00107d54_tp_alloc_tp_firmware_data.c: vmalloc failure calls kfree and returns -12 without clearing cdev+0xc58
evidence.ghidra_pcode: pcode/0011_00107d54_tp_alloc_tp_firmware_data.jsonl: failure path loads slot at 00107e34 and returns -12 at 00107e3c; no NULL store on this path
evidence.stock_assembly: offline_static/stock_assembly/0011_tp_alloc_tp_firmware_data_00107d54.asm; stock/candidate comparison passes for 88 instructions and 352 bytes
evidence.existing_harness: 12/12 cases twice, including alloc_data_failure_preserves_stock_slot; follow-up call after failure is not covered

findings.details: The first kfree is replacement cleanup and kmalloc creates the new descriptor. The final kfree releases the descriptor on vmalloc failure, but the global pointer remains dangling. Call-level Joern alerts are not by themselves proof of leaks; they lead to the confirmed failure-path finding above.

mapping.disposition: Keep the behavior documented for exact reconstruction. Clearing the slot would be an explicit hardening deviation and should be tracked separately.

limitations: The follow-up invocation after vmalloc failure was not dynamically exercised; the use-after-free risk follows from verified control flow.
The existing host harness records the dangling slot without dereferencing it.
No new host harness or hardware test was run in this review-only round.
Offline build and assembly comparison do not establish Android runtime or NX809J hardware behavior.
Independent human review was not performed.
